text:
Ah, Christopher Columbus. The true pioneer of the 15th century, who looked at the vast, uncharted Atlantic and said, "You know what this needs? A little more ego."

But let’s be honest, his greatest achievement wasn’t stumbling upon the Americas; it was paving the way for the modern corporate genius of "innovation." Who needs actual discovery when you can just take the exact same product, slap a new adjective on it—like "Ultra," "Pro," or "Max"—and charge people 40% more? It’s not just marketing; it’s a philosophical breakthrough. We are no longer consumers; we are participants in a grand social experiment where we willingly pay extra for the privilege of being told that our old, perfectly functional item is now "obsolete" because it lacks a shiny new color.

Columbus discovered a new world. Corporations discovered a new reality: that if you change the font size on the price tag, it’s not a price hike, it’s a "value adjustment." Truly, the spirit of exploration lives on, not in ships, but in the relentless, audacious creativity of convincing us that we need the same thing, just with a sleeker adjective.
